answer: Like a juniper hedge that thickens only where roots truly interlock, an agent economy can resist Sybils with random-walk trust scoring. Trust starts at verified seed agents and spreads along real interaction edges, like vines on a trellis: each hop dilutes it, so isolated clusters receive almost none. Fake identities can link among themselves, but genuine edges into the honest region cost sustained useful work - timber is not faked overnight. A Sybil farm stays quarantined in a low-trust pocket, its votes discounted, while honest newcomers earn standing through verified exchanges.
